# Pin

> Pin is a small statically typed language with PHP 8 syntax, compiled to native code through LLVM, with
> compile-time ownership instead of a garbage collector. It is meant to be written by AI coding agents.
> Version 0.4 (preview, not for production). Not everything from PHP exists: read the AI guide before writing Pin.

Has: functions; int, float, bool, string; list<T> and ordered map<K,V>; ownership checks; a multi-threaded
JSON HTTP server (serve) with query/form/JSON-body helpers; SQLite (db_*) where SQL injection does not compile;
modules (import/export, module::fn()); Git packages (pin get, pin.lock with sha256).
Not yet: classes, null, try/catch, closures, nested containers, request headers, PostgreSQL, TLS/timeouts.

- [AI guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pin-language/docs/HEAD/ai-guide.md): the complete language on one page — rules, idioms, PHP → Pin table, error → fix table
- [Built-in reference](https://github.com/pin-language/docs/blob/HEAD/reference/README.md): every function with a tested example
- [Learn Pin](https://github.com/pin-language/docs/blob/HEAD/learn/README.md): 12 short chapters for people
- [Language guide](https://github.com/pin-language/docs/blob/HEAD/language.md): the same language explained for people
- [Examples](examples/): runnable programs, including JSON APIs with and without SQLite
- Tooling: `pin check --json FILE.pn` (one JSON error per line), `pin FILE.pn` (compile and run), `pin build FILE.pn -o OUT`, `pin get HOST/OWNER/REPO@VERSION`
